title: Access port in wrong VLAN
symptom: PC1 in the Sales area gets 169.254.x.x instead of a 10.10.10.0/24 address. It cannot ping its gateway 10.10.10.1 or any host.
topology_note: SW1 Fa0/3 is patched to PC1. Sales = VLAN 10 (10.10.10.0/24), Engineering = VLAN 20 (10.10.20.0/24). Router-on-a-stick on R1 Gi0/0 with subinterfaces.
show_outputs:
SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN Name      Status    Ports
---- --------- --------- ------------------------------
10   SALES     active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2
20   ENG       active    Fa0/3, Fa0/4, Fa0/5

SW1# show interfaces Fa0/3 switchport
Name: Fa0/3
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 20 (ENG)

PC1> ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 169.254.71.4
Subnet Mask: 255.255.0.0
Default Gateway: 0.0.0.0
expected_fault: Fa0/3 is an access port in VLAN 20 but PC1 belongs to the VLAN 10 Sales segment, so its DHCP discover never reaches the Sales pool.
expected_fix_steps: SW1(config)# interface Fa0/3 | switchport mode access | switchport access vlan 10 ; then release/renew on PC1 and confirm a 10.10.10.x lease.

title: VLAN assigned to port but missing from VLAN database
symptom: Three HR PCs on SW2 have no connectivity to each other or anything else. Link lights are green.
topology_note: SW2 ports Fa0/10-12 were configured for HR VLAN 30 (10.10.30.0/24). VTP is in transparent mode so VLANs are not learned from SW1.
show_outputs:
SW2# show vlan brief
VLAN Name      Status    Ports
---- --------- --------- ------------------------------
1    default   active    Fa0/13, Fa0/14
10   SALES     active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2
20   ENG       active    Fa0/3

SW2# show interfaces Fa0/10 switchport
Access Mode VLAN: 30 (Inactive)

SW2# show vtp status
VTP Operating Mode: Transparent
expected_fault: VLAN 30 was never created in SW2's VLAN database, so the access ports show 'Inactive' and traffic is black-holed.
expected_fix_steps: SW2(config)# vlan 30 | name HR | exit ; re-verify with show vlan brief that Fa0/10-12 are listed under VLAN 30 and are no longer Inactive.

title: VLAN pruned from trunk allowed list
symptom: Sales PCs on SW1 can reach each other, and Sales PCs on SW2 can reach each other, but the two groups cannot reach across the switch uplink.
topology_note: SW1 Gi0/1 <-> SW2 Gi0/1 is the inter-switch uplink carrying VLANs 10, 20 and 30.
show_outputs:
SW1# show interfaces trunk
Port      Mode  Encapsulation  Status    Native vlan
Gi0/1     on    802.1q         trunking  1

Port      Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1     20,30

Port      Vlans allowed and active in management domain
Gi0/1     20,30

SW2# show interfaces trunk
Port      Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1     1-4094
expected_fault: VLAN 10 is not in the allowed list on SW1 Gi0/1, so Sales frames are dropped at the trunk even though both switches know VLAN 10.
expected_fix_steps: SW1(config)# interface Gi0/1 | switchport trunk allowed vlan add 10 ; confirm VLAN 10 appears under 'allowed and active' on both ends.

title: Native VLAN mismatch on trunk
symptom: Intermittent connectivity between switches and a repeating CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH console message. Management VLAN traffic leaks between segments.
topology_note: SW1 Gi0/1 to SW3 Gi0/2 trunk. Management is VLAN 99.
show_outputs:
SW1# show interfaces trunk
Port      Mode  Encapsulation  Status    Native vlan
Gi0/1     on    802.1q         trunking  99

SW3# show interfaces trunk
Port      Mode  Encapsulation  Status    Native vlan
Gi0/2     on    802.1q         trunking  1

SW1# show logging | include NATIVE
%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1 (99), with SW3 GigabitEthernet0/2 (1).
expected_fault: The two trunk ends disagree on the native VLAN (99 vs 1), so untagged frames land in the wrong VLAN — a connectivity and security problem.
expected_fix_steps: SW3(config)# interface Gi0/2 | switchport trunk native vlan 99 ; clear the log and confirm the CDP mismatch message stops.

title: Wrong default gateway on host
symptom: PC5 can ping other hosts inside 10.10.20.0/24 but nothing outside its own subnet.
topology_note: Engineering VLAN 20 = 10.10.20.0/24, gateway is R1 subinterface Gi0/0.20 at 10.10.20.1.
show_outputs:
PC5> ipconfig /all
IPv4 Address: 10.10.20.55
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 10.10.20.254

PC5> ping 10.10.20.1
Reply from 10.10.20.1: bytes=32 time=1ms TTL=255

PC5> ping 10.10.20.254
Request timed out.

R1# show ip interface brief | include Gi0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0.20  10.10.20.1   YES manual up  up
expected_fault: The host's default gateway 10.10.20.254 does not exist; the real gateway is 10.10.20.1, which the host can ping.
expected_fix_steps: Set PC5 default gateway to 10.10.20.1 (or fix the DHCP pool's default-router option if the address was leased); re-test with ping to an off-subnet host.

title: SVI administratively down
symptom: Every host in VLAN 40 lost off-subnet connectivity at once after a maintenance window. Hosts still ping each other.
topology_note: MLS1 is a layer-3 switch doing inter-VLAN routing with SVIs. VLAN 40 = 10.10.40.0/24, SVI 10.10.40.1.
show_outputs:
MLS1# show ip interface brief | include Vlan
Vlan1    unassigned    YES unset  administratively down down
Vlan10   10.10.10.1    YES manual up                    up
Vlan40   10.10.40.1    YES manual administratively down down

MLS1# show running-config interface Vlan40
interface Vlan40
 ip address 10.10.40.1 255.255.255.0
 shutdown
expected_fault: Interface Vlan40 is administratively shut down, so the gateway address for VLAN 40 is not active and no traffic is routed off the segment.
expected_next_command: show ip interface brief | include Vlan
expected_fix_steps: MLS1(config)# interface Vlan40 | no shutdown ; verify the SVI goes up/up and hosts can reach 10.10.40.1 and beyond.

title: Duplicate IP address between host and gateway
symptom: Users in VLAN 10 report connectivity that works for a few seconds then drops. A duplicate address error appeared on a workstation.
topology_note: VLAN 10 = 10.10.10.0/24. R1 Gi0/0.10 is the gateway at 10.10.10.1. A printer was statically configured last week.
show_outputs:
PRINTER> ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 10.10.10.1
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0

R1# show ip interface brief | include Gi0/0.10
GigabitEthernet0/0.10  10.10.10.1  YES manual up  up

SW1# show mac address-table | include 10.10
  10   0060.5c2a.11b3   DYNAMIC  Fa0/8
  10   00e0.f7aa.0091   DYNAMIC  Gi0/1

PC2> arp -a
  10.10.10.1   0060.5c2a.11b3  dynamic
expected_fault: The printer is statically configured with 10.10.10.1, the same address as the router subinterface. Hosts intermittently ARP-resolve the gateway to the printer's MAC.
expected_fix_steps: Re-address the printer to a free host address outside the DHCP range (e.g. 10.10.10.240) and add it to ip dhcp excluded-address; clear ARP caches and re-test.

title: Wrong subnet mask puts gateway off-subnet
symptom: A newly imaged laptop cannot reach anything, not even the gateway, although the address looks correct at a glance.
topology_note: Engineering VLAN 20 is 10.10.20.0/24 with gateway 10.10.20.1. The laptop was configured manually.
show_outputs:
LAPTOP> ipconfig /all
IPv4 Address: 10.10.20.77
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.240
Default Gateway: 10.10.20.1

LAPTOP> ping 10.10.20.1
Destination host unreachable.

LAPTOP> route print | include 10.10.20
10.10.20.64  255.255.255.240  On-link  10.10.20.77
expected_fault: A /28 mask places the laptop in 10.10.20.64/28, so 10.10.20.1 is treated as off-subnet and the host tries to route to it via a gateway it cannot reach.
expected_fix_steps: Change the mask to 255.255.255.0 (/24), or switch the host to DHCP; confirm the local route becomes 10.10.20.0/24 and the gateway pings.

title: Missing ip helper-address for remote DHCP
symptom: Hosts in VLAN 30 never get a lease and fall back to APIPA. Hosts in VLAN 10 and 20 lease normally.
topology_note: A central DHCP server at 10.10.99.10 serves all VLANs. R1 has subinterfaces Gi0/0.10, .20 and .30.
show_outputs:
R1# show running-config interface Gi0/0.30
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30
 encapsulation dot1Q 30
 ip address 10.10.30.1 255.255.255.0

R1# show running-config interface Gi0/0.20
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20
 encapsulation dot1Q 20
 ip address 10.10.20.1 255.255.255.0
 ip helper-address 10.10.99.10

PC9> ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 169.254.12.9
expected_fault: Gi0/0.30 has no ip helper-address, so broadcast DHCP DISCOVER frames from VLAN 30 are never relayed as unicast to the server at 10.10.99.10.
expected_fix_steps: R1(config)# interface Gi0/0.30 | ip helper-address 10.10.99.10 ; renew on a VLAN 30 host and confirm the lease with show ip dhcp binding on the server.

symptom: Some Sales users get addresses and some do not. The failures started after a training class of 20 extra laptops joined.
topology_note: R1 is the DHCP server for VLAN 10. The pool was sized for a small office.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip dhcp pool
Pool SALES :
 Utilization mark (high/low)    : 100 / 0
 Subnet size (first/next)       : 0 / 0
 Total addresses                : 29
 Leased addresses               : 29
 Pending event                  : none

R1# show running-config | section dhcp
ip dhcp excluded-address 10.10.10.1 10.10.10.200
ip dhcp pool SALES

 default-router 10.10.10.1
 dns-server 10.10.99.53

R1# show ip dhcp conflict
IP address     Detection method   Detection time
expected_fault: The excluded-address range reserves .1-.200, leaving only 29 usable addresses (.201-.229 after the broadcast), and all of them are leased.
expected_fix_steps: Shrink the exclusion to 10.10.10.1 10.10.10.20, or shorten the lease time; then clear ip dhcp binding * and confirm leased vs total addresses on show ip dhcp pool.

title: DHCP hands out the wrong default gateway
symptom: Hosts get an address in the right subnet and can ping each other, but nothing off-subnet works. The problem affects every host in the VLAN.
topology_note: VLAN 20 = 10.10.20.0/24, gateway 10.10.20.1. The pool was copied from the VLAN 10 pool during a config change.
show_outputs:
R1# show running-config | section dhcp pool ENG
ip dhcp pool ENG
 network 10.10.20.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 10.10.10.1
 dns-server 10.10.99.53

PC7> ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 10.10.20.31
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 10.10.10.1

PC7> ping 10.10.20.1
Reply from 10.10.20.1: bytes=32 time<1ms TTL=255
expected_fault: The ENG pool advertises default-router 10.10.10.1, an address that is not reachable on the VLAN 20 segment; the correct gateway 10.10.20.1 is up.
expected_fix_steps: R1(config)# ip dhcp pool ENG | default-router 10.10.20.1 ; clear ip dhcp binding *, renew on hosts, and confirm ipconfig shows the corrected gateway.

title: Rogue DHCP server on the access layer
symptom: Roughly half of the hosts in VLAN 10 get a 192.168.1.x address instead of 10.10.10.x. Which hosts are affected changes after each reboot.
topology_note: A user plugged a home wireless router into SW1 Fa0/22 last week. DHCP snooping is not configured.
show_outputs:
PC3> ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 192.168.1.104
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.1.1

PC4> ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 10.10.10.203
Default Gateway: 10.10.10.1

SW1# show mac address-table interface Fa0/22
  10   0001.6440.aa10   DYNAMIC  Fa0/22

SW1# show ip dhcp snooping
Switch DHCP snooping is disabled
expected_fault: An unauthorised DHCP server on Fa0/22 races the legitimate server; hosts that accept its OFFER first receive a 192.168.1.0/24 lease and an unreachable gateway.
expected_fix_steps: Disconnect or shut Fa0/22, then enable ip dhcp snooping for VLAN 10 and mark only the uplink toward the real server as trusted; renew clients and confirm all leases are 10.10.10.x.

title: No DNS server configured on host
symptom: PC6 can ping 10.10.99.20 by address but browsing to http://intranet.lab.local fails immediately.
topology_note: Internal DNS server is 10.10.99.53 and holds the lab.local zone. PC6 is statically addressed.
show_outputs:
PC6> ipconfig /all
IPv4 Address: 10.10.20.60
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 10.10.20.1
DNS Servers: 0.0.0.0

PC6> ping 10.10.99.20
Reply from 10.10.99.20: bytes=32 time=2ms TTL=126

PC6> nslookup intranet.lab.local
Non-authoritative answer:
*** Can't find server name
expected_fault: The host has no DNS server address, so name resolution fails while IP connectivity is fine — a Layer 7 problem, not a routing problem.
expected_fix_steps: Set the DNS server to 10.10.99.53 on PC6 (or move it to DHCP so it inherits the dns-server option); re-test with nslookup intranet.lab.local.

title: ACL blocking DNS on UDP 53
symptom: All VLAN 30 hosts fail name resolution. They can ping the DNS server's IP address successfully.
topology_note: An inbound ACL 130 was applied to R1 Gi0/0.30 to restrict guest-adjacent traffic. DNS lives at 10.10.99.53.
show_outputs:
PC11> nslookup www.lab.local
DNS request timed out.

PC11> ping 10.10.99.53
Reply from 10.10.99.53: bytes=32 time=3ms TTL=126

R1# show access-lists 130
Extended IP access list 130
 10 permit icmp 10.10.30.0 0.0.0.255 any (412 matches)
 20 permit tcp 10.10.30.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 80 (88 matches)
 30 permit tcp 10.10.30.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 443 (140 matches)
 40 deny ip any any (263 matches)

R1# show ip interface Gi0/0.30 | include access list
  Inbound  access list is 130
expected_fault: ACL 130 permits ICMP, HTTP and HTTPS but never permits UDP 53, so DNS queries hit the implicit-style deny at line 40 (263 matches).
expected_fix_steps: R1(config)# ip access-list extended 130 | 35 permit udp 10.10.30.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.10.99.53 eq 53 ; re-run nslookup and confirm the new line increments matches while line 40 stops growing.

title: Missing A record on the DNS server
symptom: http://files.lab.local fails from every VLAN, but http://intranet.lab.local works from the same hosts.
topology_note: Single internal DNS server 10.10.99.53 serving lab.local. The file server was re-addressed to 10.10.99.25 yesterday.
show_outputs:
PC2> nslookup intranet.lab.local
Server: 10.10.99.53
Address: 10.10.99.53
Name: intranet.lab.local
Address: 10.10.99.20

PC2> nslookup files.lab.local
Server: 10.10.99.53
*** 10.10.99.53 can't find files.lab.local: Non-existent domain

PC2> ping 10.10.99.25
Reply from 10.10.99.25: bytes=32 time=2ms TTL=126
expected_fault: The DNS zone has no A record for files.lab.local even though the host is up at 10.10.99.25; resolution of other names proves the server itself is healthy.
expected_fix_steps: Add A record files.lab.local -> 10.10.99.25 in the DNS service on 10.10.99.53; flush the client resolver cache and re-test nslookup and the browser.

title: Router name lookup fails but hosts resolve fine
symptom: An engineer typing 'ping server1' on R1 gets a translation error and a long hang. Client PCs resolve names normally.
topology_note: R1 is used as a jump point for testing. Internal DNS is 10.10.99.53.
show_outputs:
R1# ping server1
Translating "server1"...domain server (255.255.255.255)
% Unrecognized host or address, or protocol not running.

R1# show running-config | include domain
ip domain-lookup
no ip name-server

R1# ping 10.10.99.53
Success rate is 100 percent (5/5), round-trip min/avg/max = 1/2/4 ms
expected_fault: R1 has ip domain-lookup enabled but no ip name-server configured, so it broadcasts lookups to 255.255.255.255 and times out. Client-side DNS is unaffected.
expected_fix_steps: R1(config)# ip name-server 10.10.99.53 | ip domain-name lab.local ; re-run ping server1 and confirm it translates. Optionally add 'no ip domain-lookup' on lab devices to avoid typo hangs.

title: Missing return static route
symptom: Hosts on the 10.10.10.0/24 LAN cannot reach the 172.16.50.0/24 branch LAN. Pings from R1 to R2's WAN interface succeed.
topology_note: R1 (HQ) and R2 (Branch) are joined by a serial link 192.168.100.0/30. Static routing only, no dynamic protocol.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip route static
S    172.16.50.0/24 [1/0] via 192.168.100.2

R2# show ip route static
(no static routes)

R2# show ip route | begin Gateway
Gateway of last resort is not set
     172.16.0.0/24 is subnetted, 1 subnets
C       172.16.50.0 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
     192.168.100.0/30 is subnetted, 1 subnets
C       192.168.100.0 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0

PC1> tracert 172.16.50.10
 1  10.10.10.1
 2  *  *  *  Request timed out.
expected_fault: R2 has no route back to 10.10.10.0/24, so echo requests arrive but replies are dropped. The forward path is fine, which is why the trace dies after the first hop.
expected_fix_steps: R2(config)# ip route 10.10.10.0 255.255.255.0 192.168.100.1 (or a default route toward HQ); confirm with show ip route and an end-to-end ping from PC1.

title: OSPF area mismatch prevents adjacency
symptom: R1 and R3 never form an OSPF neighbour relationship. The link is up and the two WAN addresses ping each other.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip ospf neighbor
(no output)

R1# show running-config | section router ospf
router ospf 1
 network 192.168.200.0 0.0.0.3 area 0
 network 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255 area 0

R3# show running-config | section router ospf
router ospf 1
 network 192.168.200.0 0.0.0.3 area 1
 network 172.16.60.0 0.0.0.255 area 1

R1# show ip ospf interface Se0/0/1 | include Area
  Process ID 1, Router ID 10.10.10.1, Network Type POINT_TO_POINT, Cost: 64
  Area 0
expected_fault: The shared link is in area 0 on R1 and area 1 on R3. OSPF hellos are discarded because the area ID field does not match, so no adjacency forms.
expected_fix_steps: R3(config)# router ospf 1 | no network 192.168.200.0 0.0.0.3 area 1 | network 192.168.200.0 0.0.0.3 area 0 ; verify a FULL neighbour with show ip ospf neighbor.

title: Wrong wildcard mask in OSPF network statement
symptom: OSPF is up between routers, but the 10.10.20.0/24 Engineering LAN never appears in remote routing tables.
topology_note: R1 advertises three LANs plus the WAN link. Adjacency with R2 is FULL.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID  Pri  State     Address          Interface
10.10.99.1     0  FULL/  -  192.168.100.2    Serial0/0/0

R1# show running-config | section router ospf
router ospf 1
 network 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
 network 10.10.20.0 0.0.0.0 area 0
 network 192.168.100.0 0.0.0.3 area 0

R1# show ip ospf interface brief
Interface  PID  Area  IP Address/Mask     Cost  State
Se0/0/0    1    0     192.168.100.1/30    64    P2P
Gi0/0.10   1    0     10.10.10.1/24       1     DR

R2# show ip route ospf
O    10.10.10.0/24 [110/65] via 192.168.100.1
expected_fault: The wildcard 0.0.0.0 matches only the exact address 10.10.20.0, which is not assigned to any interface, so Gi0/0.20 is never enabled for OSPF and the LAN is not advertised.
expected_fix_steps: R1(config)# router ospf 1 | no network 10.10.20.0 0.0.0.0 area 0 | network 10.10.20.0 0.0.0.255 area 0 ; confirm Gi0/0.20 appears in show ip ospf interface brief and the route reaches R2.

title: No default route toward the ISP
symptom: Internal traffic between all LANs works. No host can reach 8.8.8.8 or any external address.
topology_note: R1 Gi0/1 connects to ISP router at 203.0.113.1/30. NAT is configured and appears healthy.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip route | begin Gateway
Gateway of last resort is not set
     10.0.0.0/24 is subnetted, 3 subnets
C       10.10.10.0 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.10
C       10.10.20.0 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.20
C       10.10.30.0 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.30
     203.0.113.0/30 is subnetted, 1 subnets
C       203.0.113.0 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/1

R1# ping 203.0.113.1
Success rate is 100 percent (5/5)

R1# ping 8.8.8.8
Success rate is 0 percent (0/5)
expected_fault: 'Gateway of last resort is not set' — R1 has no default route, so any destination outside the connected subnets is dropped even though the ISP next-hop is reachable.
expected_fix_steps: R1(config)# ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.1 ; confirm 'Gateway of last resort is 203.0.113.1' and ping 8.8.8.8 from R1 then from a host.

title: ACL applied in the wrong direction
symptom: An ACL intended to stop Guest VLAN 30 from reaching the server VLAN has instead blocked all traffic from the server VLAN, including replies to Sales.
topology_note: ACL 110 was written to deny 10.10.30.0/24 to 10.10.99.0/24 and was applied on R1 Gi0/0.99.
show_outputs:
R1# show access-lists 110
Extended IP access list 110
 10 deny ip 10.10.30.0 0.0.0.255 10.10.99.0 0.0.0.255 (0 matches)
 20 permit ip any any (12 matches)

R1# show ip interface Gi0/0.99 | include access list
  Outgoing access list is not set
  Inbound  access list is 110

PC-GUEST> ping 10.10.99.20
Reply from 10.10.99.20: bytes=32 time=3ms TTL=127
expected_fault: ACL 110 is applied inbound on the server subinterface, so it only sees traffic sourced from 10.10.99.0/24 and never matches guest traffic (0 matches on the deny line).
expected_next_command: show ip interface Gi0/0.99 | include access list
expected_fix_steps: R1(config)# interface Gi0/0.99 | no ip access-group 110 in | ip access-group 110 out — or better, apply it inbound on Gi0/0.30 closest to the source; re-test and confirm the deny line increments.

title: Implicit deny drops return traffic
symptom: Hosts behind R1 can send traffic out to the internet but no replies come back. Outbound counters increase, inbound sessions never complete.
topology_note: ACL 101 was applied inbound on the WAN interface Gi0/1 to filter unsolicited traffic.
show_outputs:
R1# show access-lists 101
Extended IP access list 101
 10 permit tcp any host 203.0.113.2 eq 22 (0 matches)
 20 permit icmp any any echo (0 matches)
 (implicit deny — 1874 matches shown via 'show ip access-lists 101' counters)

R1# show ip interface Gi0/1 | include access list
  Inbound  access list is 101

PC1> ping 8.8.8.8
Request timed out.

R1# show ip nat translations | count
Number of lines which match regexp = 26
expected_fault: ACL 101 has no permit for established/return traffic, so the implicit deny at the end discards echo-replies and TCP ACKs coming back from the internet.
expected_fix_steps: R1(config)# ip access-list extended 101 | 15 permit tcp any any established | 25 permit icmp any any echo-reply ; or replace the ACL with a zone-based/reflexive policy. Confirm ping and TCP sessions complete.

title: ACL rule ordering — deny placed before permit
symptom: The HR manager's PC (10.10.30.25) is supposed to be exempt from the guest restriction but is still blocked from the server VLAN.
topology_note: ACL 120 is applied inbound on R1 Gi0/0.30.
show_outputs:
R1# show access-lists 120
Extended IP access list 120
 10 deny ip 10.10.30.0 0.0.0.255 10.10.99.0 0.0.0.255 (57 matches)
 20 permit ip host 10.10.30.25 10.10.99.0 0.0.0.255 (0 matches)
 30 permit ip any any (204 matches)

R1# show ip interface Gi0/0.30 | include access list
  Inbound  access list is 120

PC-HR> ping 10.10.99.20
Request timed out.
expected_fault: ACLs are evaluated top-down. Line 10 denies the whole 10.10.30.0/24 subnet before line 20 can permit the manager's host, which is why line 20 has 0 matches.
expected_fix_steps: R1(config)# ip access-list extended 120 | no 20 | 5 permit ip host 10.10.30.25 10.10.99.0 0.0.0.255 ; re-test from PC-HR and confirm line 5 increments while line 10 still blocks other guests.

title: ACL applied to the wrong interface
symptom: A restriction meant only for the Guest VLAN is affecting Engineering users, who have lost access to the file server.
topology_note: Guest is VLAN 30 on Gi0/0.30; Engineering is VLAN 20 on Gi0/0.20.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip interface brief | include Gi0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0.20  10.10.20.1  YES manual up  up
GigabitEthernet0/0.30  10.10.30.1  YES manual up  up
